# Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- On June 26, 2025, HPS Corporate Lending Fund executed a commitment increase agreement for its senior secured revolving credit facility with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent.
- HPS Corporate Lending Fund serves as the Borrower in this transaction, with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce joining as an Assuming Lender providing a new Multicurrency Commitment.
- The original Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement was dated June 23, 2022, and has been amended multiple times (Amendment No. 1 in October 2023, Amendment No. 2 in June 2024, and Amendment No. 3 in April 2025).
- The purpose of this agreement is to increase the aggregate amount of commitments under the existing revolving credit facility through the addition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as a new lender.
- The facility includes multiple issuing banks: JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A., Bank of America N.A., Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Wells Fargo Bank National Association, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
- Strong banking consortium comprising top-tier financial institutions (JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Sumitomo Mitsui), indicating strong lender confidence
- Multicurrency facility structure provides operational flexibility for international transactions
- Multiple amendments since 2022 suggest ongoing lender support and willingness to accommodate borrower needs
- Addition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as a new lender demonstrates continued market appetite for the credit

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
- Limited visibility into overall financial performance, covenants, or pricing terms constrains comprehensive credit assessment
- Multiple amendments to the original agreement may indicate evolving credit needs or potential covenant management

- On June 26, 2025, HPS Corporate Lending Fund executed a commitment increase agreement for its senior secured revolving credit facility with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent.
- HPS Corporate Lending Fund serves as the Borrower in this transaction, with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce joining as an Assuming Lender providing a new Multicurrency Commitment.
- The original Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement was dated June 23, 2022, and has been amended multiple times (Amendment No. 1 in October 2023, Amendment No. 2 in June 2024, and Amendment No. 3 in April 2025).
- The purpose of this agreement is to increase the aggregate amount of commitments under the existing revolving credit facility through the addition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as a new lender.
- The facility includes multiple issuing banks: JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A., Bank of America N.A., Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Wells Fargo Bank National Association, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
- Strong banking consortium comprising top-tier financial institutions (JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Sumitomo Mitsui), indicating strong lender confidence
- Multicurrency facility structure provides operational flexibility for international transactions
- Multiple amendments since 2022 suggest ongoing lender support and willingness to accommodate borrower needs
- Addition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as a new lender demonstrates continued market appetite for the credit

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
- Limited visibility into overall financial performance, covenants, or pricing terms constrains comprehensive credit assessment
- Multiple amendments to the original agreement may indicate evolving credit needs or potential covenant management
